title: manteen configuration
description: Consumer configuration for manteen. Lives at <project root>/manteen.json; its directory IS the project root. manteen never reads components.json — the aliases here are import-path prefixes backed by tsconfig `paths`, which is a different thing from shadcn's alias map.

$schema.description: Declared so `additionalProperties: false` does not reject the field that gives you editor completion.

registries.description: Namespace -> where its items live. The namespace is what you type in `manteen add @house/data-table`.

propertyNames.description: A namespace: `@` followed by lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Matches the `namespace` field of the authoring catalog that produced the registry.

aliases.description: Import-path prefixes files are placed under. All four are required, and each must be backed by a `paths` key in your tsconfig — content ships verbatim, so a project whose tsconfig cannot resolve the prefix gets files that install cleanly and do not compile.

theme.description: Path to your Mantine theme, relative to this file. Items that ship a theme file or a theme fragment are folded into it rather than written alongside it. Need not exist yet.

styles.description: Path to the Manteen-owned composed package stylesheet, relative to this file. Consumer overrides belong in a host stylesheet imported after it.

tsconfig.description: Path to the tsconfig whose `paths` back the aliases, relative to this file. Defaults to ./tsconfig.json. Resolved verbatim — name the file, not its directory.

resolutions.description: Which registry wins when two of them publish the same item name. Durable, because the decision has to survive CI. The value's item name must equal the key.

propertyNames.description: A bare item name — no namespace, no leading slash.

registrySource.description: Either the item URL template on its own, or an object when the registry also publishes an index or needs headers or query parameters.

index.description: URL of the registry index. Used for did-you-mean on a 404. Declared rather than inferred from `url`, because substituting name="registry" only happens to work for one emitted layout.

headers.description: Sent with every request to this registry. Values may reference environment variables as ${VAR}; expansion happens when the request is made, never in anything stored or printed.

params.description: Appended to every request URL as a query string. Same ${VAR} rule as `headers`.

urlTemplate.description: Where one item lives, with the literal {name} standing in for the item's name — for example https://example.com/r/{name}.json. Required rather than guessed: appending /{name}.json to a base URL produces a 404 that reads as a missing item whenever the guess is wrong.

alias.description: An import-path prefix such as @/components/ui — the thing that appears in an import specifier. Not a filesystem path.
